policy: Curated metadata and original summaries only. Access levels are explicit; no restricted paper scraping or full-paper reproduction.

sources.title: Who sets the price of gold? London or New York
sources.source: Journal of Futures Markets 36(6), 564-586; University of Edinburgh repository
sources.access_reviewed: Repository abstract and bibliographic record only; full paper not reviewed.
sources.market_dataset: London spot and New York gold futures; 17 years of intraday observations.
sources.methodology: Comparative price-discovery analysis; full estimator specification requires paper review.
sources.key_findings: Both venues contribute; futures contribute more on average, with variation by time and liquidity.
sources.limitations: Historical venue comparison; not a test of broker CFDs or order-block entries.
sources.gold_applicability: Direct gold context, without an intraday profitability claim.
sources.hypothesis: H02 session heterogeneity; separate future synchronized spot/futures study.

sources.title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
sources.source: Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1), 47-88; arXiv revision 2011
sources.access_reviewed: Public HTML abstract, introduction and model sections consulted; not a full replication.
sources.market_dataset: US equity trades and quotes/order-book event observations.
sources.methodology: Relate short-horizon price changes to order-flow imbalance and market depth.
sources.key_findings: Price changes are related to order-flow imbalance; impact depends on depth.
sources.limitations: Equities, not gold; OHLCV cannot reconstruct additions, cancellations or trade aggressor direction.
sources.gold_applicability: Motivates a future gold quote/depth study; candle volume is not OFI.
sources.hypothesis: H04 is only a candle-volume proxy; real OFI testing is blocked without event data.

sources.title: Commitments of Traders: Explanatory Notes
sources.market_dataset: Aggregated reportable futures positions by trader business classification.
sources.methodology: Regulatory reporting and category aggregation, not an alpha study.
sources.key_findings: Disaggregated categories distinguish producer/merchant, swap dealer, managed money and other reportable participants.
sources.limitations: Categories are not identities, intentions or real-time orders; spreading positions are separate.
sources.gold_applicability: Use COMEX gold code 088691 and futures-only archives; never mix combined options series.
sources.hypothesis: H05 positioning context at weekly horizon only.

sources.title: COT Release Schedule and Historical Compressed Archives
sources.access_reviewed: Release schedule, archive index and variable names consulted.
sources.market_dataset: Annual disaggregated futures-only CSV archives across contracts.
sources.methodology: Observation date and public release are distinct; archives are downloadable ZIP files.
sources.key_findings: Usual release is Friday 15:30 Eastern for preceding Tuesday; holidays can delay releases.
sources.limitations: A tentative schedule is not proof of actual publication; finalized archives can contain revisions.
sources.gold_applicability: Explicit publication evidence or conservative retrieval-time availability is required.
sources.hypothesis: H05; historical conclusions require release and vintage audits.

sources.title: Gold Futures Contract Specifications
sources.source: CME Group official product documentation; checked 2026-10-18
sources.access_reviewed: Public product page inspected; dynamic specification fields were not fully exposed.
sources.market_dataset: COMEX listed gold futures product documentation.
sources.methodology: Exchange contract reference, not empirical research.
sources.key_findings: Gold futures are a listed exchange product with contract-specific trading and delivery terms.
sources.limitations: No contract-size or fee values imported from incompletely exposed fields. Yahoo rolling proxy rules require separate verification.
sources.gold_applicability: Do not transfer futures contract terms to broker XAU/USD CFD sizing.
sources.hypothesis: H07 execution stress tests require verified venue-specific costs.

sources.title: Time Series Momentum
sources.source: Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 228-250; author-affiliated AQR summary
sources.access_reviewed: Public author-affiliated summary only; full paper not reviewed.
sources.market_dataset: 58 futures/forward instruments across asset classes over more than 25 years.
sources.methodology: Predict returns with instruments' own past returns at multi-month horizons.
sources.key_findings: Summary reports trend persistence and later partial reversal.
sources.limitations: Monthly/annual effects do not establish H1 BOS or M15 confirmation profitability.
sources.gold_applicability: Indirect motivation to test trend rather than assume a gold intraday effect.
sources.hypothesis: H01 H1 alignment, explicitly a new hypothesis.

sources.title: When do stop-loss rules stop losses?
sources.source: Journal of Financial Markets 18, 234-254; MIT repository
sources.access_reviewed: MIT repository abstract and citation only; full paper not reviewed.
sources.market_dataset: Daily index-futures prices and buy-and-hold exposure policies.
sources.methodology: Analytical framework and empirical evaluation of stop-loss overlay policies.
sources.key_findings: Some policies at longer sampling frequencies can improve expected return and reduce volatility.
sources.limitations: Portfolio exposure policies differ from zone-boundary trade stops; effect is not universal.
sources.gold_applicability: Indirect methodology lead; needs gold-specific execution data.
sources.hypothesis: H07 predefined cost and stop sensitivity; not parameter selection on the final test.

sources.title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
sources.access_reviewed: Public PDF abstract and introductory methodology excerpts consulted; no full replication.
sources.market_dataset: Strategy-selection framework and illustrative performance experiments.
sources.methodology: Combinatorially symmetric cross-validation to quantify strategy selection overfitting.
sources.key_findings: Selecting from many backtests can produce misleading historical winners.
sources.limitations: PBO requires comparable candidate return histories; it is not a significance certificate.
sources.gold_applicability: General research design, independent of instrument.
sources.hypothesis: All hypotheses: log variants; consider PBO only if candidate matrix justifies it.

sources.title: yfinance.download API documentation
sources.market_dataset: Yahoo-provided historical instruments; GC=F used as gold-futures proxy.
sources.methodology: Unofficial Yahoo wrapper with explicit adjustment, repair and missing-row options.
sources.key_findings: Intraday availability is limited; documentation states 60 days generally. Actual limits vary and must be checked per request.
sources.limitations: No guarantee of completeness, latency or proxy roll construction; personal-use/access terms apply.
sources.gold_applicability: Exploratory futures data only; not broker spot CFD history or institutional order flow.
sources.hypothesis: Data pipeline validation, not evidence for any trade hypothesis.
